definitions.explanation: The hottest period of summer, typically referring to July and August in Japan. A somewhat literary or formal word for the peak of the summer season.

examples.japanese: {盛夏|せいか}の{候|こう}、いかがお{過|す}ごしですか。
examples.english: In this midsummer season, how are you doing?
examples.notes: A formal seasonal greeting used in letters.

examples.japanese: {盛夏|せいか}を{迎|むか}え、{気温|きおん}が{三十五度|さんじゅうごど}を{超|こ}える{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: With midsummer upon us, temperatures exceeding 35 degrees have continued.

examples.japanese: {盛夏|せいか}にはビールの{売|う}り{上|あ}げが{伸|の}びる。

notes: A literary word often seen in seasonal greetings ({時候|じこう}の{挨拶|あいさつ}) and written correspondence. {盛夏|せいか}の{候|こう} is a set phrase used in formal summer letters. Compare with {真夏|まなつ} (midsummer — more colloquial), {猛暑|もうしょ} (fierce heat), and {酷暑|こくしょ} (extreme heat). A homophone of {成果|せいか} (result), {聖火|せいか} (sacred flame), and {製菓|せいか} (confectionery), but written with different kanji.
